decisive_items: increased CD8+ T count with inverted CD4:CD8 ratio
response.rationale: Thymoma-associated multiorgan autoimmunity best explains the oral lichenoid/interface dermatitis, diarrhea, recurrent infections, hypogammaglobulinemia, and CD8-predominant infiltrate in the setting of a type AB thymoma. Negative pemphigus serology and absence of skin involvement exclude pemphigus vulgaris; lack of epidermotropic atypical lymphocytes and cutaneous plaques excludes mycosis fungoides.

rejected.why: Pemphigus vulgaris would require suprabasal acantholysis and intercellular IgG on direct immunofluorescence or positive indirect immunofluorescence; here DIF showed only fibrinogen, indirect IF and ELISA were negative, and skin was spared.
Mycosis fungoides would show epidermotropic atypical lymphocytes and cutaneous involvement; the oral-only lichenoid pattern with thymoma and immunodeficiency is not consistent with mycosis fungoides.
